analyst_view.overall: Early view: City come out of the break on three straight league defeats under Enzo Maresca, the latest a 3-1 loss at Forest in which Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol were both taken off injured at half-time. Fulham are unbeaten in four league games under Arbeloa, with 1-1 draws at Villa and against Newcastle. City should still have most of the ball, but the fitness of their centre-backs is the team news to watch.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, 2.2 of them for City. I lean a little lower: City have scored once in their last two league games (1-0 defeat to Brighton, 3-1 at Forest), and Fulham's last two matches both ended 1-1. The risk the other way is City's defence, which conceded twice in the first 18 minutes at Forest and may be without Guehi.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.2 corners, 6.1 of them for City. I lean higher: after three league defeats City should throw men forward at home, and a Fulham side that has been grinding out draws is likely to defend deep and clear plenty of balls behind. Doku taking on full-backs one-on-one is a regular source of them.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards, 2.5 of them on Fulham. I lean slightly lower: Fulham were not booked at all in the 1-1 with Newcastle, and a side defending in a settled low block at the Etihad gives away fewer tactical fouls than one that presses. The referee has not been named yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.8 shots, 16.4 of them City's. I lean slightly higher: City will be desperate to end a three-game league losing run and Fulham are likely to concede possession, which pushes City's attempts up. Antoine Semenyo is out with a knee injury until December, but Haaland and Cherki still give them plenty of shooters.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. I lean a little lower: a deep Fulham block gets bodies in front of many efforts, and City's finishing has been off, with one league goal in two games. An early City goal would change the shape of this.
